To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intracerebroventicular injection of arginine vasotpressin (AVP), acting on V1 receptors, activates the sympathetic system, increases blood pressure and decreases baroreflex sensitivity.
central AVP, by activating V1 receptors in the brain and by activating the sympathetic nervous system and inhibiting vasodilator mechanisms, increases arterial pressure.
the central cardiovascular actions of vasopressin and the role of the hormone in the modulation of the baroreflex sensitivity are investigated in conscious rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the brain vasopressin system in the control of cardiovascular functions.
the central cardiovascular actions of AVP and the role of the peptide in the modulation and regulation of baroreceptor sensitivity.
the role of the brain renin-angiotensin system (RAS) in the regulation of cardiovascular function in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cardiovascular actions of AVP are complex.
central AVP acts on V1-AVPRs to increase blood pressure, whereas circulating AVP acts on peripheral and central V2-AVPRs and on peripheral V1-AVPrs to increase BRR sensitivity.
the central pressor action of AVP is mediated by the V1-AVP subtype of the receptor, whereas the peripheral pressor effects are mediated by the V2-AVP subtype of receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the central actions of AVP on blood pressure, sympathetic nerve activity, and baroreflex sensitivity are mediated through the V1-AVP-receptor, and that the central actions may be modulated by the circulating (peripheral) AVP acting on the V2-AVP-receptor.
AVP is a potent central pressor agent and that its central actions are mediated by V1-AVPreceptors.
central V1-AVP and peripheral V2-AVP act in concert to maintain the blood pressure and to adjust BRR sensitivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AVP is a multifunctional hormone that can act as a central neurotransmitter and as a peripheral hormone.
AVP is not only a potent vasopressor but also a modulator of baroreflex sensitivity.
AVP is a multifunctional peptide that acts on different receptor subtypes and can be released in the central nervous system and peripherally.
